scope: The 12 investigation families in the project catalogue. Supporting physics, ventilation, instrument and flamelet references are not separate catalogue investigations. No raw PSI run files were imported.
method: Reading-priority ranking: direct topic match = 3, related = 1, background = 0. Scores are authored relevance judgments, not measured performance, safety or research quality. Equal scores share competition ranks; alphabetical order only arranges ties.

understand.name: ACME · CFI-G
understand.reason: Explores oxygen-rich conditions, but an inverse burner is different from a crew cabin atmosphere.
understand.objective: Investigate cool flames with gaseous fuels in an inverse flame arrangement.
understand.checkedScope: NASA identifies CFI-G as the gaseous-fuel cool-flame investigation; it is separate from droplet CFI.
understand.limits: The 85% oxygen figure and detailed inverse-burner configuration from the challenge brief were not independently checked in this audit. They are not imported as verified conditions.

understand.name: ACME · E-FIELD Flames
understand.reason: Useful for studying transport effects. Electrically driven flow does not provide direct lunar-gravity combustion data.
understand.objective: Study how an electric field moves ions and changes gas flow around a flame.
understand.checkedScope: Electric fields act on flame ions and induced gas motion; the research concerns control of non-premixed flames.
understand.limits: Overview claims only. No raw run data, apparatus settings or performance guarantees imported.

understand.name: Cool Flames Investigation (CFI)
understand.reason: Helps explain why disappearance of a visible hot flame may not mean all combustion has stopped.
understand.checkedScope: CFI concerns cool-flame chemistry; NASA operations groups it under MDCA. NASA connects the later gas experiment to the earlier FLEX droplet observations.
understand.limits: No CFI dataset identifier, temperatures or species measurements imported. CFI and CFI-G remain separate.

understand.name: DAFT / DAFT-2
understand.reason: Useful for understanding shared sensing hardware and non-fire aerosols; not a combustion investigation.
understand.objective: Assess aerosol measurements for dust detection.
understand.checkedScope: NASA’s PSI index lists DAFT and DAFT-2. NASA’s DAFT description links its modified P-Trak instrument to SAME.
understand.limits: Instrument relationship is described at overview level. DAFT-2-specific settings and smoke/dust calibration are not checked.

understand.reason: Relevant to solid-material flammability questions despite using a gaseous-fuel burner.

understand.name: BASS / BASS-II

applications.checkedScope: BASS-II studies solid-fuel burning in MSG; oxygen, airflow and sample geometry are test variables. The report identifies imaging and gas measurements.
applications.limits: BASS-II record only; BASS-I runs are not individually checked. No numerical run files or calibration have been imported.

applications.name: DAFT / DAFT-2
applications.reason: Useful for understanding shared sensing hardware and non-fire aerosols; not a combustion investigation.
applications.objective: Assess aerosol measurements for dust detection.
applications.checkedScope: NASA’s PSI index lists DAFT and DAFT-2. NASA’s DAFT description links its modified P-Trak instrument to SAME.
applications.limits: Instrument relationship is described at overview level. DAFT-2-specific settings and smoke/dust calibration are not checked.

applications.name: Saffire-I / II / III
applications.reason: Relevant to fire spread in crew-sized environments and to the limits of small-sample tests.
applications.objective: Study solid-material fire behaviour at a larger scale than small laboratory samples.
applications.checkedScope: Saffire I–III investigate large-scale material flame spread and flammability. Saffire-I was conducted in Cygnus after departure from ISS.
applications.limits: Direct repository link covers Saffire-I, not the full I–III family. Measurements and sample dimensions have not been imported.

applications.name: SAME / SAME-R
applications.reason: Directly informs how different smoke sources affect a detector’s signal.
applications.objective: Characterise smoke and investigate fire detection in microgravity.
applications.checkedScope: SAME examined material-dependent smoke and detector response. SAME-R is a reflight with changed materials, conditions and instrumentation.
applications.limits: The repository record is SAME-R; the publication covers spacecraft detector testing. Do not merge the two test matrices. No response curves or detector specifications are imported.
